# Bundled pictures

157 pictures drawn for a 32×32 panel, 24 of them animated GIFs. `index.json`
lists them with an id, a display name and a category.

**Do not edit these files by hand.** They are generated by
`tools/build_gallery.py` in the repository root, which also rewrites the
dropdown in `services.yaml`. Running it again overwrites anything changed here.
To alter a picture, change its drawing function and re-run:

```
python tools/build_gallery.py --sheet /tmp/sheet.png
```

## Licence

Every picture is drawn by code in this repository using nothing but rectangles,
lines, circles and polygons. The few motifs carrying a word — STOP, the speed
limit, ON AIR — use a 3×5 face defined pixel by pixel in `tools/pixelart.py`,
not an imported font file. Nothing is traced and no third-party image set is
used, so the gallery carries the repository's GPL-3.0 licence like the rest of
the source.

## Why 32×32

Pixel art does not scale the way vector art does: a motif drawn to read at
32×32 turns to mush at 16 pixels and goes blocky at 64. The panels this
integration supports come in thirty different geometries, so one bundled set
cannot fit them all. 32×32 was chosen because it is the most common square
size, and because `show_gallery_image` defaults to `fit`, which scales the
whole picture down and pads with black rather than cropping a slice out of the
middle on a wide panel.

Motifs that depend on a *value* — battery level, a gauge, a progress ring — do
not belong here. Those are drawn at the panel's own reported size at the moment
they are needed.
